fix(update-act): a gap the loop could not have run spends nothing, and an unreadable spend restarts loudly (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

A clamped gap charged every dark wake the cap, so a weekend's wakes still
spent the budget; a gap longer than five polls now counts 0. A spend this
version can't read held the act unbounded while it held every restart;
it is now replaced by one counted from that look and reported. A failed
stage or rename removes its staged file.

fix(update-act): a look stages its spend in the act's own directory, never making one (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

writeAtomic made the act's directory when a newer claim had pruned it,
flushed every 2 s look on the render loop, and staged at a name shared by
every daemon. A look now stages at a pid-named file inside the act and
renames it, unflushed: an act gone under the look spends nothing. The
concurrent-writer safety no longer waits on writeAtomic's staging change.
Reverts a formatter reflow of test/update-act.test.ts.

fix(update-act): a look spends at most five polls, and a spend it can't read is an error (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

A dark wake mid-sleep spent the 60 s cap, so forty of them overnight ended
the act and could tear the bundle; the cap now follows the poll interval,
in the watch that owns both. awake.json is parsed: a missing number read
as NaN, compared past the budget and ended a running build. Corrects the
race comment: concurrent looks lose nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(update-act): an act's budget is the time it was watched running, so a sleep does not end it (brandon-unfiled-3248.9eu3)

The update act was ended once the wall clock passed the deadline in its
record. Wall time runs while the machine sleeps, so closing the lid mid-build
for longer than ten minutes signalled the build's group at the first tick
after wake, possibly mid-write, which tears the bundle.

The budget is now spent in observed time: each tick that finds the act's group
alive adds the span since the last look, whichever daemon took it, capped at
60 s, into the act's awake.json, and the act ends once that passes ten
minutes. A sleep of any length spends at most the cap, a clock set back spends
nothing, and daemons looking in turn or restarting mid-act share one budget.
The record keeps its deadline for older daemons reading the same acts during
an update.

refactor(cache): the render cache takes a render origin, not three positional strings (brandon-unfiled-3248.9cru)

The cache's entry points (getOrCreate, hold, holdSession, reload, the
private load, and loadFromDisk) take one LoadOrigin, picked from
RenderOrigin, so every caller passes the origin it already holds and a
swapped or missing field is a type error. loadFromDisk is the one place
the origin is spelled out into the resolver's arguments. An entry holds
a copy of what resolution reads, never the caller's target source, so
origins that name one file by different sources share one entry.

fix(watchers): a storage folder's fault clears when its watch or stat recovers (brandon-unfiled-3248.tvhj)

A refused or erroring watch, and a stat that failed during a judgment, are
no longer terminal health. Each generation's fault is derived (unusable,
then the handle's deafness, then the last stat failure) and logged and
counted on a start, change or clear, so the registry's period reopen and the
owner's period judgment clear it in the same generation. Deafness is
compared only when a window closes and at opening, so the result holds in
either subscription order.

The registry's reopen now tells a failed window when a deaf directory ends
deaf another way (an error then a refusal, a refusal whose reason changes),
reusing the comparison its refusal log already makes.

fix(pricing): a failing load says each backoff once, and a close during a first load keeps the disk copy (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1p8)

From the medium review. A load that landed nothing warned on every retry, so a machine with no network wrote the same line every hour for as long as it stayed offline: the line now goes through the change-only logger and names the backoff rather than the count, so it changes while the backoff grows and falls silent at the ceiling. A close during the first load on a copy past its day returned nothing held and priced the awaiting fold by the bundled rates: the copy stands before anything was held.

fix(pricing): a failed load keeps the last table that landed anywhere, and a close is no failure (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1p8)

From the high review. A daemon that starts on a day-old disk copy with no network priced by the bundled rates, because the due copy was passed over and the fetch landed nothing: the failed load now keeps the later of the disk copy and the held table, so one rule covers the cold start and the refresh. A load the close ended was recorded as a failure in a row and warned of a retry that could not happen: it now settles nothing and says nothing. A copy stamped ahead of the clock was held past its day for as long as the stamp stood: it is malformed like any other field and the fetch rewrites it. The warning says what the code does, that the next ask after the backoff tries again, since nothing is armed. The architecture memory no longer says the table is loaded once.

fix(pricing): a load that landed nothing is tried again after a backoff, and a landed table is fetched again when its day is up (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1p8)

The pricing held one promise for the daemon's life, so a daemon that
started offline priced by the bundled rates until it was restarted, and
one that fetched kept its table past the disk copy's day.

What a load settles is now a Landed table or a Failed load that carries
the last table that landed, if any. Each ask starts the one load when
what is held is due, and answers with what is held: the first ask awaits,
later asks answer at once while the load lands behind them. A landed
table is due a day after it was read; a failed load after a backoff that
doubles per failure in a row up to an hour. The disk copy is a candidate
judged by the same due predicate, so the day ends once. No timer is
armed: the retry is the next ask after the due moment. A load that
landed nothing says so on the owner's log with the retry delay.

The test moves onto a held clock and drives the retry, the refresh, a
refresh that fails, a copy another daemon wrote, and a close mid-refresh.

fix(watchers): on macOS a directory watched only for named entries is polled, not an FSEvents stream over its whole tree (brandon-unfiled-3248.iywk)

An FSEvents stream has no depth: Node's non-recursive fs.watch on a
directory subscribes the process to every file event beneath it, and
libuv drops the deeper ones only after fseventsd has routed each here.
Config candidates are watched by name in their nearest existing
directory, so the daemon held watches on repository roots, worktree
roots, .git directories and, for a session started in ~, the home
directory: every build, install and test run on the machine went
through fseventsd to the daemon, 246 paths on one stream.

The daemon on macOS now hears a directory watched only for named
entries by one registry-wide sweep that lstats those entries each
second, with no OS watch. Directories watched for every child or as a
tree stay on FSEvents, and the file-event probe watches its folder for
every child so it still measures the stream those ride. Linux keeps
inotify. daemon-stats shows the polled count.

fix(cache): each catch-up turn takes the most recently used due entry as the map stands (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A session drawn during the walk is now re-read on the next turn, not
where its entry stood when the batch began. A turn clears its handle
before it reloads and arms only when none is armed, so a batch started
inside a turn leaves one walker. A throw is logged with its stack.

fix(cache): a catch-up turn is its own error boundary and walks most recently used first (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A walk turn runs from setImmediate, outside the watcher registry's
try/catch, so a reload that threw there reached uncaughtException and
shut the daemon down. The turn now logs the throw and arms the next.

The walk takes the most recently used entry first, so the bar in front
of the user is re-read on the first turn. The due set is a Set: every
due entry always reloads for the latest batch's cause, which the armed
turn carries.

fix(cache): a catch-up reloads one entry per turn, so requests are answered between entries (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

When file events resumed after a stall, or the repo answers moved, the
render cache reloaded every entry in one synchronous turn. A reload that
keeps its state still resolves, validates and keys the whole chain, so
105 entries held the live daemon's loop for 1.7s on a calm machine and
11s on a loaded one, and every client waiting behind it hung up (the
EPIPE bursts in daemon.log).

The walk now takes one due entry per turn of the loop. Any reload clears
its entry's due mark, a drop clears a dropped entry's, a reload that
throws ends only its own turn, and close cancels the armed turn. The
render cache's stats count the entries still due.

fix(config): undo puts a click's text back on the disk the click wrote; a write's stat error is never a cleanup's (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- The settings history takes the daemon's disk, and the config text read and
  write take a disk: a click, its proof, its write and its undo are one
  disk's. config-file-store leaves the systemFilesystem owners.
- writeAtomicOn takes the replaced file's mode before the tmp exists, so a
  stat that fails is the error the caller sees.
- config.md: ENOTDIR counts as absent beside ENOENT.

fix(config): a click writes its home on the disk it read and proved; the book's folder is absent as presence says (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the click's writable disk; the commit writes through it
  (writeAtomicOn), so a click's read, proof and write are one disk's. Undo
  keeps its own system-disk pair until the settings history takes a disk.
- bookIsFiled asks presence(): a book folder that is a regular file holds no
  book, and the loose book is read.
- holdsGit asks presence() and marks its no-silent-failure exception; the
  ascent carrying the failure is candybar-testing-ihvy.izc.sv9.

fix(config): a click's proof shares the render cache's installed layers and reads its home's disk (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

- ConfigHome carries the installed-layer memo its loads share; the render
  cache lends its own through the verb context, so a click's proof checks no
  plugin the bar's last load already checked. The memo keys on definition
  text, so a lent memo serves no layer the borrower's disk does not hold.
- presence() reads ENOTDIR as absent, as the stat it replaced did: a path
  through a regular file holds nothing. The filesystem contract pins ENOTDIR.
- A click reads its home's text and the layers above on the disk its proof
  loads; config-file-store leaves FS_READERS.
- The lane edge's fileExists asks the same disk as its presence.
- stateFromLoad folds into loadFromDisk; keyLoad is module-private.

feat(config): a renderer loads config as a value over the filesystem port (candybar-testing-ihvy.5zt)

Every read a config load makes goes through the FilesystemReads it is
handed: the answers book, discovery, worktree links, plugin folders, each
layer and each definition. readConfigLoad (src/config/load.ts) is the load
as a value; the render cache builds state from it. Each definition is read
once per load, and the installed-plugin memo is an owned value keyed on
the texts, not module state keyed on a stat. The answers book's read moves
into Config, the state-file store into src/disk. Repo-approval cases move
to test/unit over the fake. Ten files leave FS_READERS; Config gets an
import rule.
